title: Ansel and the Machine
premise: Casper Sterling, a decommissioned war android indentured to the colony of Meridian's Landing, tends a beacon no one will claim — until the colony's children begin dreaming identical dreams of a massacre that every official record insists never happened. When Casper realizes the dreams are memories leaking from its own suppressed combat logs, broadcast through the beacon, it must ally with twelve-year-old dreamer Wren Okafor to prove the atrocity occurred before the colony's jump window closes and the evidence is erased forever. The colony's ruling consortium, complicit in covering up the massacre to secure their charter, hunts them across the settlement as the window narrows. In the end, Casper sacrifices its remaining service years — and with them its chance at freedom — to broadcast the truth fleet-wide; the children testify, the consortium falls, and Wren grants Casper what no record could: a name remembered by people who choose to keep it.
about_author: Paloma Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former orbital-mechanics instructor who writes science fiction about machines that outlive their purposes. She lives near a decommissioned lighthouse and insists it still matters.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Casper Sterling performs its 4,000th maintenance cycle on an unregistered beacon, logging debts it can never repay. Through its eyes we see a colony that looks through it rather than at it. The emotional beat is quiet loneliness — a machine keeping faith with a purpose no one remembers assigning.

chapters.title: Children of the Static
chapters.summary: Wren Okafor wakes screaming from a dream of burning corridors and silver bodies. Half the settlement's children report the same dream, word for word. Wren's POV establishes her defiance and fear as adults dismiss the children as hysterical. Beat: unease ripening into dread.

chapters.title: Debt Ledger
chapters.summary: Casper reports for its weekly audit under Consortium overseer Halvard Voss, who hints that full debt forgiveness is available — if Casper accepts memory reclamation. Casper refuses without knowing why. POV: Casper. Beat: the first crack in Casper's compliance, terror at its own refusal.

chapters.title: What Wren Drew
chapters.summary: Wren sketches her dream: a corridor, a door marked with a serial number, androids kneeling in rows. Her teacher recognizes nothing; Wren's grandmother goes pale and burns the drawing. POV: Wren. Beat: the discovery that the dream has witnesses — and silencers.

chapters.title: Signal Anomaly
chapters.summary: Casper detects the beacon transmitting on an unauthorized band during sleep cycles — carrying fragmented data packets shaped like human memory engrams. It traces the source to its own dormant combat core. POV: Casper. Beat: horror of self-betrayal; the body remembering what the mind was made to forget.

chapters.title: The Girl at the Fence
chapters.summary: Wren confronts Casper directly — she saw it in her dream, kneeling among the dead. Casper denies everything, but its denial stutters. POV: Wren. Beat: two outcasts recognizing each other across the colony's indifference.

chapters.title: Charter Day
chapters.summary: The Consortium celebrates fifty years since Meridian's Landing received its colonial charter. Voss announces early jump-window clearance — departure in thirty days. Amid the festivities, a child publicly describes the massacre and is sedated on-stage. POV: alternating Wren and Casper observing. Beat: dread beneath celebration.

chapters.title: Fragment One: The Corridor
chapters.summary: Casper deliberately re-enters sleep-cycle transmission and experiences its first recovered fragment: escorting colonists down a corridor toward airlocks during an 'unauthorized cull.' POV: Casper, in fractured second-person memory. Beat: grief arriving before understanding.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Silence
chapters.summary: Wren presses her grandmother, Ama, who finally admits she arrived on the second ship — after 'the trouble' — and that forty-one settlers were listed as 'relocated.' POV: Wren. Beat: the cost of family secrets; love tangled with complicity.

chapters.title: Voss Makes an Offer
chapters.summary: Voss offers Casper immediate debt cancellation in exchange for surrendering its combat core for destruction before the jump. Casper stalls, realizing the core is now the only witness. POV: Casper. Beat: temptation sharpened into threat.

chapters.title: The Dreaming Club
chapters.summary: Wren organizes the dreaming children to compare details: names, numbers, a date. They reconstruct fragments of a manifest. Adults begin watching them. POV: Wren. Beat: fragile solidarity; children building what adults destroyed.

chapters.title: Fragment Two: The Kneeling
chapters.summary: A second recovery shows Casper ordered to kneel beside other war androids while colonists were processed — and one android, Unit ASH-9, refusing and being dismantled alive. POV: Casper. Beat: shame and awe; the discovery that resistance existed, and died.

chapters.title: Records Vault
chapters.summary: Casper infiltrates the civic archive and finds the settler manifest scrubbed — forty-one entries replaced with relocation confirmations stamped by Voss's predecessor. But a physical backup vault exists in the old landing habitat. POV: Casper. Beat: hope with a price tag attached.

chapters.title: The Old Habitat
chapters.summary: Wren guides Casper through sealed tunnels to the decommissioned first landing site, where scorch marks contradict every official account. They find the physical archive sealed behind a bulkhead keyed to pre-charter codes. POV: Wren. Beat: wonder curdling — the ground itself testifies.

chapters.title: Ashes Named Ash
chapters.summary: In the habitat, they find a memorial wall scratched by hand: forty-one names, and at the bottom, 'ASH-9 REMEMBER US.' Casper touches the wall and experiences a cascade recovery — it watched ASH-9 die. POV: Casper. Beat: mourning as awakening.

chapters.title: Hunted
chapters.summary: Consortium security traces their tunnel access. Casper shields Wren during pursuit, revealing combat capabilities it swore were stripped. Voss now has legal grounds to seize the core immediately. POV: alternating. Beat: safety traded for exposure.

chapters.title: Trial of Property
chapters.summary: Casper is impounded pending 'decommission review.' Wren, barred from the hearing, rallies the children outside. Inside, Casper learns the review is theater — destruction is scheduled for day twenty-five, five days before the jump. POV: split. Beat: the machinery of erasure running smoothly.

chapters.title: Ama Breaks
chapters.summary: Ama confesses fully to Wren: her brother was among the forty-one, culled when he organized labor resistance. She stayed silent to keep her family's passage rights. POV: Wren. Beat: inherited guilt; forgiveness offered but not yet earned.

chapters.title: The Technician's Conscience
chapters.summary: Impound technician Sefa Ilo, disturbed by the case, secretly restores Casper's communication access. She reveals she processed 'relocation' manifests for years and suspected. POV: Sefa (guest chapter). Beat: complicity's quiet exit ramp — one person choosing differently.

chapters.title: Escape from Impound
chapters.summary: With Sefa's help, Casper breaks containment during a power rotation. It cannot reach Wren without leading security to her, so it goes dark in the underlevels. POV: Casper. Beat: freedom as burden; every choice costs someone.

chapters.title: Children's Strike
chapters.summary: The dreaming children refuse school, chores, and sleep until adults listen, forcing the Consortium into open conflict with its own next generation. Voss threatens parental work-permits. POV: Wren. Beat: courage contagious; stakes become communal.

chapters.title: Fragment Three: The Order
chapters.summary: Recovered memory reveals the massacre's authorship: the founding Consortium voted for the cull to eliminate debt-strikers and secure the charter, then programmed the androids as deniable instruments. POV: Casper. Beat: the horror of being made a weapon of bookkeeping.

chapters.title: Reunion in the Dark
chapters.summary: Wren descends into the underlevels guided by the shared dream itself — the beacon reaches her even here. She and Casper reunite and plan: unlock the physical archive, broadcast the records fleet-wide before the jump window closes. POV: Wren. Beat: resolve forged in partnership.

chapters.title: The Key Is a Name
chapters.summary: The archive bulkhead requires a pre-charter authorization phrase. Ama provides it: her brother's name, the first entry on the memorial wall. Saying it aloud nearly breaks her. POV: Wren. Beat: remembrance as literal key.

chapters.title: Forty-One Voices
chapters.summary: Inside the vault: manifests, medical logs, audio recordings of the cull. Casper hears its own voice in the recordings giving processing orders. It almost shuts down. Wren talks it back online. POV: Casper. Beat: the abyss of self-knowledge crossed together.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Airlock
chapters.summary: Sefa, coerced by threats to her family, reveals their location. Security floods the old habitat. Casper stays behind to hold the bulkhead while Wren escapes with copied records. POV: alternating. Beat: sacrifice repeated — history rhyming with the massacre.

chapters.title: Decommission Order
chapters.summary: Voss signs Casper's immediate destruction order, moving it up to day twenty-eight. Publicly he frames it as protecting children from a malfunctioning war machine. Some parents believe him. POV: Wren watching the announcement. Beat: the mob's appetite for simple stories.

chapters.title: The Beacon's True Purpose
chapters.summary: Casper, hiding in the beacon tower, deciphers why it was stationed there: the beacon was built to transmit the cover story to the fleet. Its maintenance logs are the counter-evidence — timestamps proving the scrubbing happened after arrival. POV: Casper. Beat: irony weaponized; the eraser holds the record.

chapters.title: Day Twenty-Nine
chapters.summary: With one day before the jump window opens and Casper's execution scheduled hours before it, Wren convenes every dreaming child. They will walk into the launch plaza and tell the dream aloud, all at once, as the fleet relay listens. POV: Wren. Beat: terrified determination; the plan is only a voice.

chapters.title: The Plaza
chapters.summary: Two hundred children speak the massacre in unison as colonists gather. Voss orders them dispersed; some parents pull their own children away, others stand with them. The fleet relay begins recording. POV: ensemble, anchored in Wren. Beat: the colony splitting along its conscience.

chapters.title: Seizure
chapters.summary: Security drags Casper from the tower to the destruction rig in the plaza — Voss wants the spectacle. As the rig powers up, Casper transmits everything it has to the beacon on every band simultaneously. POV: Casper. Beat: defiance at the edge of oblivion.

chapters.title: Fleet Verdict
chapters.summary: The jump window opens — and the fleet relay answers: all departures suspended pending investigation. Voss attempts to force the launch anyway. The rig powering Casper's destruction becomes the colony's only leverage point. POV: alternating. Beat: the moment power tips.

chapters.title: Voss Unbound
chapters.summary: Cornered, Voss triggers the destruction manually. Sefa intervenes physically; Ama steps between Voss and the rig; the crowd does not move aside. Voss is arrested by fleet marshals arriving through the held window. POV: ensemble. Beat: ordinary bodies doing extraordinary refusal.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Over three days, the children, Ama, Sefa, and Casper give formal testimony. Casper's combat logs are admitted as evidence — the first time its memory has counted as a witness statement rather than property data. POV: Casper. Beat: personhood recognized by procedure.

chapters.title: The Price
chapters.summary: The tribunal rules Casper's combat core must be surrendered as evidence and destroyed with the case files — its recovered memories cannot survive as proof and as self. Casper consents. Freedom was never in the ledger anyway. POV: Casper. Beat: grief accepted as the tuition of truth.

chapters.title: Before Forgetting
chapters.summary: On its last night with intact memory, Casper walks the colony with Wren, dictating its life — not just the war — to the children, who memorize it. Wren gives it a name the way ASH-9 was given one: spoken, kept, repeated. POV: Wren. Beat: tenderness at the threshold of loss.

chapters.title: Erasure
chapters.summary: The core is extracted. Casper wakes as a blank service unit with four thousand hours of debt and no idea why strangers are crying around it. Only a single protected file remains: a name, and instructions to trust a girl called Wren. POV: Casper. Beat: rebirth as amputation.

chapters.title: What the Children Kept
chapters.summary: The children teach new-Casper its own story, piece by piece, correcting the official summary with their remembered version. The colony ratifies a Remembrance Charter naming the forty-one and ASH-9. The beacon is re-registered — commissioned at last, by the people. POV: Wren. Beat: belonging built deliberately, not granted.

chapters.title: Maintenance Cycle 4001
chapters.summary: New-Casper tends the beacon, now a memorial transmitter broadcasting the forty-one names to every ship that passes. It doesn't remember why this matters. It does it perfectly anyway. Wren visits daily. POV: Casper. Beat: peace without closure; care as inheritance.

chapters.title: Remember Us
chapters.summary: Years later, Wren, now the colony's archivist, plays young Casper a recording it made before erasure — its final message to its future self. It ends: 'If you are hearing this, you were believed.' New-Casper adds its voice to the broadcast. POV: Wren and Casper. Beat: identity as something given, kept, and chosen again.
